title: Sprint-Slice Forecast & Commitment Lanes for Hosted API + Model Catalog — Q3 Scenario Plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
Redwood needs a compact, scenario-driven quarterly plan for the Hosted API + Model Catalog that maps delivery commitments to economic and capacity realities. We observed three recent friction points: (1) surprise scheduled model swaps that affected latency guarantees for mid-tier customers, (2) uneven capacity hedges during seasonal bursts, and (3) lack of a lightweight commitment taxonomy for product + infra to align on canaries and fallbacks.

Goal:
Create a repeatable 'Sprint-Slice Forecast' that: (a) defines three commitment lanes (Reserve, Flex, Evictable) for model variants and endpoint guarantees; (b) produces a schedule for Q3 that balances customer SLAs, Dedicated capacity hedges, and hosted cost targets; (c) surfaces guardrails for canary windows, rollback triggers, and eval set coverage so PM/Eng/Design can approve rollouts quickly.

Success metrics (quarter):
- 90% of hosted model rotations executed within the committed window and with telemetry tags for canary exposure.
- <10% of rotations producing material latency regressions (>25% p95 increase) across monitored endpoints.
- 12% reduction in unexpected dedicated burst spend by applying capacity hedges to the Flex lane.
- OKR alignment: contributes to PM-OKR-2025-1.2 (Model stability at scale).

Scope (in-scope):
- Roadmap items and sprint slices that affect Hosted API model lineup and model catalog gating for Q3.
- Commitment lane definitions and acceptance criteria for each lane.
- Canary scheduling process and minimal telemetry requirements (traces, p95, error rate, token-cost delta).

Out of scope:
- Private/VPC on-prem deployment changes (separate roadmap).
- Deep model retraining or architecture changes outside serving-time decisions.

Proposed commitment lanes (minimal definitions):
- Reserve (Pin): Guaranteed model version for committed customers/tiers. Requires 2-week runway, capacity reservation, SLA notes, and explicit release window.
- Flex (Adaptive): Best-effort model variant with capacity hedges and automated rollback window. 72-hour canary, metrics gating, cost-sensitivity profile.
- Evictable (Opportunistic): Short-lived model experiments that may be preempted under high load and are limited to non-SLA routes. No capacity reservation; telemetry sampling mandatory.

Quarter timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (planning): finalize lane definitions, OKR targets, and slice owners.
- Week 2-4 (engineering spike): implement telemetry tags, canary toggles, and basic autoscaling policies for Flex lane.
- Week 5-8 (canaries): run two staged canaries (small cohort, medium cohort) for top 4 candidate variants.
- Week 9 (review): cross-functional sign-off and scheduling of Reserve pins for customers.
- Week 10-12 (rollouts & remediation): execute rotations, apply hedges, document outcomes.

Rollout & gating checklist (must be filled before promotion to Reserve):
- PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sprint-Slice+Forecast+Q3
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Model-Catalog-Commitments
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pulls?q=ref%3APM-40321
- Telemetry: p95, mean latency, error rate, token-cost delta, customer-facing regression tests (baseline prompts).
- Eval coverage: one representative prompt suite per top-3 endpoints.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Flex lane autoscaling underestimates tail latency -> Mitigation: conservative autoscale floor + 72-hour extended canary if tail signals exceed thresholds.
- Risk: Product teams push mid-quarter for Pins -> Mitigation: enforce monthly pin windows and require business case doc and capacity estimate.
- Risk: Observability blind spots for ephemeral Evictable variants -> Mitigation: mandatory lightweight traces + sampling hooks.

Stakeholders and owners:
- PM lead: Aisha Patel (creator) — defines acceptance criteria and customer tradeoffs.
- Eng lead: Priya Rao — runtime changes for telemetry and autoscale hooks.
- Design: Marco Silva — UX for rollout controls in Console.
- Reliability: Nora Kim — SLO implications and incident playbooks.

Decision log (summary):
- 2025-06-12: Agreed to three-lane taxonomy to keep commitments granular; captured in PRD (see link above).
- 2025-06-15: Engineering proposed a minimal telemetry schema that adds a single header tag and a canary route flag; accepted with follow-up to document sampling rates.
- 2025-06-17: Design approved a compact console widget for lane selection and manual override for canaries.

Next steps (owner -> action):
- Liam Chen -> schedule engineering spike (Week 2), add ENG tickets for autoscale floor and canary flagging.
- Priya Rao -> define telemetry schema doc and draft ENG- dependency list.
- Marco Silva -> prototype Console widget and publish Figma link.
- Aisha Patel -> finalize OKR mapping and customer comms template.

Artifacts and dashboards:
- Canary dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hostedapi/canary-overview
- Cost model spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Forecast-Q3-HostAPI
- PRD: Confluence link above

Notes on trade-offs:
- We prioritize latency/regression stability over aggressive cost-optimization for Reserve lanes. For Flex, we accept modest cost variance to retain SLA safety.
- The taxonomy intentionally separates business commitments (Reserve) from iterative experimentation (Evictable) to reduce mid-quarter friction.
